collector.timeout_cross_check: client > statement+lock enforced; INTEGER-ONLY timeouts (fractional values refused, never silently rounded)

cases.name: normal
cases.detail: one JSON document; both tables; single snapshot identity; scope check: no credentials/env/business tables in output

cases.name: lock conflict
cases.detail: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocker held; --lock-timeout-ms 500 refused the collector bounded (<5s, stderr LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR lock timeout); blocker kept its lock; zero collector connections/transactions/queries survived (pg_stat_activity residue empty after excluding blocker and fixture backends); retry after release succeeded

cases.name: connection failure
cases.detail: real in-container connection refusal (PGPORT=1 forwarded to the fixture container psql); bounded <15s, LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR

cases.name: garbage output
cases.detail: non-JSON psql output → LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR; stdout never a plausible document

cases.name: server-side statement kill
cases.detail: statement_timeout=400ms with pg_sleep(30): server cancelled (57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout), transaction aborted, no sleeping query and no idle-in-transaction survived

cases.name: server-side lock kill
cases.detail: lock_timeout=400ms under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE: canceling statement due to lock timeout; blocker unaffected

cases.name: prod-transport job teardown
cases.detail: SCOPE-PRECISE: the client kill may leave the exec-d psql inside the container alive; the SERVER-side bounds end it — asserted against pg_stat_activity that the in-container query disappears within statement+lock bound and no aborted transaction survives (real prod channel, not a child-process return assertion)

cases.name: staging prod-channel run
cases.detail: the staged SINGLE-file collector (node --check + run, no repository context) actually executes through docker compose exec -T db against the fixture

cases.name: offline adapter exit contract
cases.detail: exit 0 = PASS, exit 1 = real BLOCK verdict, exit 2 = input refusal (MISSING_INPUT/INVALID_INPUT) before any evaluation

cases.name: guard rejection zero-change
cases.detail: foreign-nonce and marker-less dedicated databases are refused; rows, schemas and the instance database list are snapshotted identical BEFORE and AFTER the rejected guard calls (both sides unchanged)

cases.name: client-kill proof (prod transport)
cases.detail: the wedged transport forwards the REAL statement to the container in the background (fd3 preserves stdin across the async list): the collection backend is captured by EXACT pid while waiting on the blocker lock; the collector exit at ≈2s proves the CLIENT timeout fired (the wedge can only be killed); the captured pid vanishes within the server-side bound (pid-precise, no query-text approximation); no aborted transaction survives

cases.name: offline CLI contract
cases.detail: REAL CLI runs per counterexample: PASS=0; BLOCK=1 with the true failure list (legacy_missing); 14 refusal counterexamples each exit 2 with their specific MISSING_INPUT/INVALID_INPUT reason

cases.name: full-chain contract (no production network)
cases.detail: the materialized chain runs end to end through the local transport against the fixture container: normal (exit 0, collection + both evaluations + summary + host evidence), BLOCK (exit 1, real verdict, evidence retained, no FAILURE marker), refusal (exit 2, FAILURE.txt stage=bind), crash (exit 3, FAILURE.txt + transport stdout/stderr archived)

cases.name: dual fixed-SHA binding
cases.detail: wrong pinned main SHA refused at bind, exit 2, FAILURE.txt stage=bind; both inventories source_ref must equal the bound refs

cases.name: hung transport timeout + unified cleanup
cases.detail: transport runs in its own process group; on the injected bound the WHOLE GROUP is SIGKILLed; chain exits 3 with failure evidence; pgrep proves no survivor

cases.name: sentinel zero-modification across all entries
cases.detail: sentinel dedicated database byte-identical after normal/BLOCK/refusal/crash entries; instance database set changes only by the chain own database

cases.name: independent remote filesystem
cases.detail: DEPLOY_PATH and host evidence under a separate root; runner evidence tree has NO host files, stdout-only recovery; remote evidence stays in the remote root

cases.name: retired-registry input refusals
cases.detail: REAL CLI runs: not-an-array, malformed entry, duplicate identity — each exits 2 with INVALID_INPUT: retired registry reason

boundaries.note: defaults in the collector; verification exercised the same code paths with shortened values

guards.dedicated_database: test refuses any database outside ^ledger_collect_ BEFORE connecting (phoenix_erp probe refused)
guards.same_instance: the URL database must exist on the specified container AND both views must report the identical server identity before anything runs
guards.staging_prod_transport: the staged SINGLE-file collector is actually RUN through its prod channel (docker compose exec db) against the fixture in scripts/ci/ledger-collection-staging.test.mjs

shared_guard.note: identity + dedicated namespace + same-instance ownership + THIS-RUN ownership nonce (ledger_fixture_owner.run_nonce verified through BOTH the container psql and the URL connection) — every fixture suite runs it before anything destructive; provisioning flows through the container channel only

cases: clean fixture: rehearsal exit 0 with PREFLIGHT_RESULT=PASS and SEMANTICS=AGREE
injected fault (LEDGER_REHEARSAL_FAULT=drop-legacy-row): rehearsal exit 1, PREFLIGHT_RESULT=BLOCK with legacy_missing, EXPECTED_PREFLIGHT_VERDICT_UNMET — the gate is live, not decorative

claim_accuracy.residue_claims: CHANNEL-SCOPED AND MEASURED: ci-channel residue assertions exclude the blocker/fixture backends by pid; the prod channel after a client kill relies on the SERVER-side bounds — now verified by the client-kill proof with exact backend pid
claim_accuracy.static_vs_dynamic: static pins (workflow YAML shape, tally assertions) are labelled static; every guard/gate/classifier/chain behavior listed here has a dynamic test

chain.stages: clean deps, source binding with dual fixed SHA (collector digest + pinned main SHA), staging, stdout recovery with a REMOTE-OWNED evidence dir the runner never reads, raw digest verification, both-side evaluation, exception archiving
chain.outcomeClasses: normal=0 / BLOCK=1 / refusal=2 / crash=3 / transport timeout=3 with process-GROUP kill and unified cleanup
chain.independentRemote: the contract test runs the host side under a SEPARATE filesystem root; the runner tree contains stdout-recovered artifacts only
chain.zeroModification: a sentinel database on the same instance is proven byte-identical across ALL four chain entries
